title: Apply resource protection in operations
question: How is data/media protected, moved, retained, and exited across provider boundaries?
scenario: A provider is returning encrypted backup drives at contract end and offers a generic destruction letter without listing serial numbers or destruction method.
focalRelation: media/data copy --use/transfer/storage/reuse/disposal state--> control obligation custody transfer --named sender/receiver and evidence--> accountability provider service boundary --divides operation, not customer accountability--> shared responsibility legal/retention need --governs--> disposal eligibility destruction --scope and remanence verification--> closure

nodes.label: Encrypted backup drives
nodes.detail: Named physical media containing protected data; encryption does not remove custody or disposal duties.

nodes.label: Provider custodian
nodes.detail: Named provider role holding the drives under shared contractual responsibilities.

nodes.label: Transfer record
nodes.detail: Time, sender, receiver, condition, transport protection, and destination for each custody handoff.

nodes.label: Serial-number inventory
nodes.detail: One-to-one reconciliation between physical drive, data scope, retention state, key status, and required outcome.

nodes.label: Destruction process
nodes.detail: Approved sanitization or physical destruction method appropriate to media, classification, and residual data risk.

nodes.label: Verification evidence
nodes.detail: Serial-specific method, performer, date, result, exceptions, retained copies, and accountable acceptance.

lanes.label: Media in scope
lanes.rule: Each encrypted drive remains a protected asset until its final disposition is verified.

lanes.rule: Every transfer names sender, receiver, time, condition, and destination.

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: A provider is returning encrypted backup drives at contract end and offers a generic destruction letter without listing serial numbers or destruction method.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: Media includes removable devices, tapes, disks, printouts, mobile devices, and cloud or virtual representations.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: Encryption makes media disposal unnecessary. Keys can leak, algorithms or configuration can fail, and metadata or residual copies may remain; disposal and custody still require control.

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Match the evidence to the media and data classification. Confirm chain of custody, key status, serials, sanitization or destruction method, provider responsibilities, retained copies, and verification. If the generic letter cannot prove the required outcome, use a controlled destruction or compensating process before closing the contract.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given a resource and lifecycle event, select protection, custody, handling, cloud-responsibility, and disposal controls that preserve confidentiality, integrity, availability, and recoverability. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

variants.label: Changed case
variants.changedFact: A SaaS provider cannot confirm where tenant backups are stored or when deleted records leave all replicas.

states.title: Changed case fact isolated
states.caption: A SaaS provider cannot confirm where tenant backups are stored or when deleted records leave all replicas.

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Treat this as a material lifecycle and recovery gap; require evidence, contract controls, or a different design before placing sensitive data there. Unknown copies undermine retention, destruction, privacy, and incident response decisions.

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

prediction.prompt: How is data/media protected, moved, retained, and exited across provider boundaries?

options.label: Encryption makes media disposal unnecessary.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Keys can leak, algorithms or configuration can fail, and metadata or residual copies may remain; disposal and custody still require control.

options.label: Accept the generic destruction letter as proof that every returned drive was destroyed.
options.feedback: Incorrect: copy-specific custody and disposition need serials or other accountable identifiers, transfer records, method, authority, exceptions, and evidence tied to the affected media.

options.label: Match the evidence to the media and data classification
options.feedback: Correct for this scenario: this answer uses the displayed relation and preserves its scope. Keys can leak, algorithms or configuration can fail, and metadata or residual copies may remain; disposal and custody still require control.

prediction.hint: Name the controlling relationship and the point where its result must be enforced; do not rely on a label or successful prior step.

transfer.prompt: A SaaS provider cannot confirm where tenant backups are stored or when deleted records leave all replicas.

options.label: Treat this as a material lifecycle and recovery gap
options.feedback: Correct. Treat this as a material lifecycle and recovery gap; require evidence, contract controls, or a different design before placing sensitive data there. Unknown copies undermine retention, destruction, privacy, and incident response decisions.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: The changed fact is “A SaaS provider cannot confirm where tenant backups are stored or when deleted records leave all replicas.” Reusing the earlier conclusion skips the changed condition and the model’s is held by named provider custodian relation.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: This bypasses the named decision owner and leaves Verification evidence unverified. Treat this as a material lifecycle and recovery gap; require evidence, contract controls, or a different design before placing sensitive data there. Unknown copies undermine retention, destruction, privacy, and incident response decisions.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A destruction certificate lists a media batch but no device serials, method, date, or custody handoff. What does it prove?

options.label: Accept it as proof that every device in inventory was destroyed
options.feedback: Without serials and custody linkage, the certificate cannot establish which media the vendor handled.

options.label: Reconcile media identity and custody; obtain method and verification evidence
options.feedback: Correct. A generic batch statement cannot prove disposition of each governed item.

options.label: Remove the media records because a vendor certificate ends the organization’s custody duty
options.feedback: Disposition evidence closes inventory only when identity, method, outcome, and custody reconcile.

retry.hint: Match the artifact to the exact media and disposition claim it is supposed to support.

takeaway: Match the evidence to the media and data classification.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 5 stable ledger states: Encrypted backup drives is held by named provider custodian Provider custodian; Provider custodian records each transfer and condition Transfer record. The model keeps Encrypted backup drives, Provider custodian, Transfer record, Serial-number inventory, Destruction process, Verification evidence distinct. Its changed case is “A SaaS provider cannot confirm where tenant backups are stored or when deleted records leave all replicas.” and every option returns to a named repair state.
